questions.question: What is the most common finding in blood testing for those with SLE? [cite: 2987]
questions.explanation: Due to SLE being an autoimmune disease and immune complex formation, complement levels are reduced. Anti dsDNA is specific but only seen in about a third of patients. RF is evident in about 30 to 50 per cent. Anticardiolipin can be evident and evidences the presence of antiphospholipid syndrome. [cite: 5267, 5268, 5269, 5270]

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature on X-ray of Rheumatoid Arthritis? [cite: 2993]
questions.explanation: Periarticular osteopenia is a characteristic Xray feature. Loosers zones are seen in osteomalacia. Osteophytes are seen in osteoarthritis. [cite: 5272, 5273, 5274]

questions.question: A patient with polymyalgia rheumatica is on a reducing dose of steroids. She is has just dropped from 10mg to 9mg however has had a flare of her symptors. What is the next course of action? [cite: 2999, 3000, 3001]
options: B- Increase prednisolone to 15 mg and slow rate of reduction [cite: 3003]
E- Increase prednisolone to 10 mg and slow rate of reduction [cite: 3006]
questions.explanation: In those who have a flare, it is important not to increase the dose back to the high doses. The steroids should be increased up one notch and then the reduction of dose tried at a slower rate. [cite: 5276, 5277]

questions.question: What disorder is most commonly associated with Raynauds Phenomenon? [cite: 3007]
questions.explanation: Raynauds phenomenon is most commonly seen in Systemic Sclerosis and less commonly SLE. It can also be seen in other disorders such as PAN and polymyositis, rheumatoid arthritis, dermatomyositis and cold agglutinin disease. [cite: 5279, 5280]

questions.question: A patient has developed nephrotic syndrome and a renal biopsy is performed. This reveals deposits in the mesangium and capillaries which stain pink with congo red and appear as green birefringence when under polarised light. What is the likely underlying diagnosis? [cite: 3014, 3015, 3016]
questions.explanation: The renal biopsy is findings are of amyloidosis and rheumatoid arthritis can lead to secondary amyloidosis. The other options do not lead to the findings described. [cite: 5282, 5283]

questions.question: Rheumatoid factor is most commonly which immunoglobulin class? [cite: 3022]
questions.explanation: The most common immunoglobulin class of RA is IgM but they can also be a of the IgA and IgG class. [cite: 5285]

questions.question: Which of the following carries the highest risk of developing SLE? [cite: 3028]
questions.explanation: The greatest risk is with monozygotic twins. HLA B27 is associated with seronegative spondylarthropathies. [cite: 5287]

questions.question: A 25 year old female complains of chest pain. She is known to have a history of SLE.Examination reveals no abnormality. There is evidence of diffuse ST elevation on an ECG. What due to you think is the likely cause of her chest pain? [cite: 3034, 3035, 3036, 3037]
questions.explanation: Pericarditis is the most common process in SLE and would explain the widespread ST elevation. Myocarditis is less common. STEMI is very unlikely. Libman-Sacks Syndrome is a non-infective endocarditis occurring in SLE. You would expect to hear a murmur. It is rare. [cite: 5289, 5290, 5291]

questions.question: A 39 year old presents with malaise, myalgia and weight loss. She has had a cough and recurrent haemoptysis. She has also noticed a rash. On examination there is evidence of palpable purpura. ANCA PR3 and ANCA MPO are positive and an eosinophil count is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis? [cite: 3044, 3045, 3046, 3047]
questions.explanation: Microscopic polyangiitis given the history and the positivity of ANCA.PR3 and ANCA.MPO. These autoantibodies are also observed in Churg-Strauss but there is also an associated eosinophilia. These autoantibodies are less common in Wegeners granulomatosis. Goodpastures anti GBM is found and the history is not indicative of PAN. [cite: 5293, 5294, 5295]

questions.question: What tissue is the most commonly involved in Wegeners Granulomatosis? [cite: 3053]
questions.explanation: Wegeners granulomatosis affects the upper respiratory tract and lungs in 90% of cases as it most commonly presents as rhinorrhoea then nasal mucosal ulceration and cough, haemoptysis and pleuritic pain. Renal tissue is affected in 80% of cases, musculoskeletail system in 60%, gastrointestinal tract in about half of cases and the skin is less commonly involved with only 40% affected. [cite: 5297, 5298, 5299]

questions.question: A 35 year old presents with pain in both his femurs. He has a history of coeliac disease. An X-ray is performed and shows Loozers zones. Which test would be most useful in confirming the diagnosis? [cite: 3059, 3060, 3061]
questions.explanation: The X-ray findings and history of osteomalacia makes the most likely diagnosis, osteomalacia, due to malabsorption of vitamin D. A rise in ALP is he most common abnormality seen. Although a low to normal calcium may be seen and a raised PTH due to a secondary hyperparathyroidism. Vitamin D and phosphate levels are low. All tests are useful however in the diagnosis. [cite: 5301, 5302, 5303]

questions.question: In a patient with rheumatoid arthritis, what is the most likely cause of a low hemoglobin with a normal MCV, normal WCC and platelet count? [cite: 3068]
options: A-Iron deficiency anaemia secondary to NSAIDS [cite: 3069]
questions.explanation: Anaemia of chronic disease such as RA leads to a normochromic, normocytic anaemia as seen here. Iron deficiency due to NSAID use and consequent Gl blood loss which can complicate the picture. Ferritin is not useful in diagnosing IDA in RA due to it being an acute phase response., Feltys Syndrome leads to splenomegaly and pancytopenia. Methotrexate also leads to pancytopenia or neutropenia more commonly. [cite: 5305, 5306, 5307, 5308]

questions.question: A 50 year old female presents with weight gain. On further questioning she complains of cold intolerance, tiredness, arthralgia and she has noticed her hair and nails becoming more brittle and her mood has been low. On examination she is bradycardic and mildly oedematous. Bloods reveal a normochromic normocytic anaemia. What test should be performed to confirm the diagnosis? [cite: 3074, 3075, 3076, 3077]
questions.explanation: The signs and symptoms described are indicative of hypothyroidism and thus a TSH should be measured to confirm the diagnosis. Cushings lead to similar changes but not bradycardia. The rest are not specific. [cite: 5310, 5311]

questions.question: What is the most common respiratory complication in SLE? [cite: 3083]
questions.explanation: The most common respiratory complication of SLE is pleural effusions. Pneumonitis and atelectasis can also occur. Restrictive lung disease then develops. Obstructive lung disease is not seen. [cite: 5312, 5313]

questions.question: A 10 year old girl presents with a one week history of malaise, joint pains and pyrexia. On examination there was evidence of a swollen erythematous knee. Her ankle had been similar a few days previously but this had now settled. What is the most likely diagnosis? [cite: 3089, 3090, 3091, 3093]
questions.explanation: Rheumatic fever is the most likely diagnosis and is usually caused by a Group A streptococcal infection. The history is indicative with a fleeting migratory polyarthritis affecting the large joints. In Stills disease the arthritis is not as fleeting and is more persistent in the affected joints. In juvenile idiopathic arthritis it is classically the small joints involved at the outset and there is no associated pyrexia. The patient is too young for a diagnosis of Rheumatoid. The fleeting nature is not suggestive of a septic arthritis. [cite: 5315, 5316, 5317, 5318, 5319]

questions.question: What antibody in SLE suggests severe systemic involvement? [cite: 3099]
questions.explanation: In SLE, dsDNA antibodies are found in about a third of cases and if often is associated with more severe systemic disease. ANA is non-specific. Anticardiolipin is associated with antiphospholipid syndrome. [cite: 5321, 5322]

questions.question: What tissue is most commonly affected in SLE? [cite: 3104]
questions.explanation: The most common tissue affected in SLE are the joints, being affected in > 90%. It commonly presents similarly to rheumatoid arthritis affecting the small joints symmetrically however the joints are usually clinically normal. The skin is affected in 35%. Up to 60% have lung involvement. In less than a third of cases are the kidneys affected. [cite: 5325, 5326, 5327, 5328]

questions.question: What is the earliest clinical finding in Ankylosing Spondylitis? [cite: 3110]
options: D- Lumbar lordosis retention during flexion [cite: 3114]
questions.explanation: The earliest finding is retention of lumbar lordosis during spinal flexion followed by paraspinal muscle wasting. Due to costochondritis there can be a reduction in chest expansion. [cite: 5330, 5331]

questions.question: What clinical finding is most commonly found in the hands of a patient with rheumatoid arthritis? [cite: 3116, 3117]
options: A- Ulnar deviation of the MCPs [cite: 3119]
questions.explanation: The most common deformity is ulnar deviation of the MCPs and palmar subluxation. [cite: 5333]

questions.question: A 19 year old male is complaining of back pain. It is stiff in the morning and the pain and stiffness eases with exercise. What are you likely to find on clinical examination? [cite: 3124, 3125, 3126]
options: C- Tenderness over the thoracic spine [cite: 3129]
E- Tenderness over the sacroiliac joint [cite: 3131]
questions.explanation: The likely diagnosis is ankylosing spondylitis which leads to sacroiliitis thus the clinical finding of tenderness over the sacroiliac joint. The other options are not indicative of ankylosing spondylitis. [cite: 5336, 5337]

questions.question: What organism most commonly leads to septic arthritis? [cite: 3132]
questions.explanation: Staph. Aureus is the most common organism to lead to septic arthritis. H. influenzae infection is often seen in children. Strep. Species are the next most common cause after staph. aureus. N. gonorrhoea can lead to septic arthritis but is more rare. [cite: 5339, 5340, 5341]

questions.question: A 42 year old gentleman has had chronic problems with rhinitis. He has just been recently diagnosed with asthma. He has had a few episodes of haemoptysis. He also has a purpuric rash. Bloods revealed an eosinophilia and autoantibodies revealed a positive PANCA and CANCA. CXR shows interstitial shadowing reported as pneumonitis. What is the most likely diagnosis? [cite: 3138, 3139, 3140, 3141]
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is Churg Strauss Syndrome which often presents as the triad of rhinitis, asthma and eosinophilia. Positive ANCA.PR3 and -MPO is also very suspicious of Churg -Strauss syndrome. It affects small and medium sized vessels. Wegeners granulomatosis can present with rhinorrhoea, cough, haemoptysis, pleuritic pain and renal symptoms such as haematuria. Eosinophilia is not seen. The history and autoantibodies are not in keeping with SLE. Polyarteritis nodosa is ANCA negative and does not normally involve the lungs. TB is not in keeping with this. [cite: 5343, 5344, 5345, 5346, 5347]

questions.question: What is the most common aetiological factor in Carpal Tunnel Syndrome? [cite: 3148]
questions.explanation: The majority of cases are idiopathic. [cite: 5348]

questions.question: What is the most common gastrointestinal complication seen in SLE? [cite: 3154]
questions.explanation: Mouth ulcers are the common Gl complication in SLE. [cite: 5349]

questions.question: A 20 year old presents with lower back pain which is worse in the morning and is associated with stiffness. It is relieved with exercise. What would most likely be seen on Lumbar spine X-ray? [cite: 3160, 3161, 3162]
options: C- Blurred upper and/or lower vertebral rims at the thoracolumbar junction [cite: 3165]
questions.explanation: You should suspect ankylosing spondylitis and thus due to enthesitis at the intervertebral ligament insertion, blurring of the vertebral rims at the thoracolumbar junction are seen. Syndesmophytes are then formed followed by fusion and sclerosis of the sacroiliac joints. Calcification of intervertebral ligaments can also occur later. [cite: 5351, 5352, 5354]

questions.question: What is the best therapy for a man with severe psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis with significant deformity? [cite: 3168, 3169]
questions.explanation: Etanercept is an antitumour necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-a) agents is very effective in severe disease and arthritis mutilans. It is utilized after 2 failed DMARDs. Methotrexate and sulfasalazine are also effective. [cite: 5356, 5357]

questions.question: What is the most common finding on the hands of a patient with psoriasis other than the skin findings? [cite: 3176, 3177]
questions.explanation: The most common finding is nail dystrophy such as pitting and onycholysis. The arthritis usually affects the DIPs when present and arthritis mutilans is rare. [cite: 5359, 5360]

questions.question: What drug therapy should be utilized in an acute attack of gout? [cite: 3183]
questions.explanation: NSAIDs such as diclofenac should be utilized for an acute attack. Colcichine and prednisolone are useful alternatives for those in which NSAIDs are contraindicated such as renal impairment or peptic ulcer. Colcichine used to be utilized as a first line. However its effectiveness is much reduced as the attack goes on and it can lead to diarrhoea and vomiting. Allopurinol is used for long term prevention and should not be used in an acute attack and should be covered by NSAIDs. Sulfinpyrazone is utilized as a prophyactic agent when allopurinol is not tolerated. [cite: 5362, 5363, 5364, 5365, 5366]

questions.question: A 60 year old woman presents nonspecifically unwell with fever and weight loss. She feels pain and stiffness in her shoulders and hips. She has also noticed she has a temporal headache and she has noticed her scalp tender when brushing her hair. Her ESR is raised. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis? [cite: 3189, 3190, 3191, 3192]
questions.explanation: The history and raised ESR is indicative of Giant cell arteritis with associated Polymyalgia Rheumatica. Polymyositis can lead to proximal muscle pain and weakness however is not associated with headache. The other options do not explain all the features. [cite: 5368, 5369, 5370]

questions.question: Which of the following is the most important factor in achieving peak bone mass? [cite: 3198, 3200]
questions.explanation: Genetic factors are the most important. All the other options do also play a role. [cite: 5372]

questions.question: What is the most common course that rheumatoid arthritis follows? [cite: 3206]
questions.explanation: The common course is chronic persistent with relapses and remissions, [cite: 5374]

questions.question: What is the most common cause of the high urate levels in gout? [cite: 3212]
options: A- Reduced renal excretion of uric acid [cite: 3213]
B- Reduced removal of uric acid by the liver [cite: 3214]
E- Increased production of uric acid [cite: 3217]
questions.explanation: In the majority of patients there is reduced renal excretion of uric acid. Often this may be due to diuretic use [cite: 5376, 5377]

questions.question: A 32 year old is on long term steroids. She presents with left hip pain and on examination there is restricted movement of abduction and internal rotation. Considering the most likely diagnosis, what investigation would be most useful to confirm it? [cite: 3218, 3219, 3220, 3221]
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is avascular necrosis of the femoral head due to the history of long term prednisolone. MRI in the early stages is most likely to confirm the diagnosis. [cite: 5379, 5380]

questions.question: A 60 year present with a swollen left painful knee. She is known to have rheumatoid arthritis, being treated with methotrexate and hydroxychloroquine. She feels unwell and is pyrexial. On examination the knee is very warm, swollen and movement of knee is very restricted. Her bloods show raised inflammatory markers and a normochromic, normocytic anaemia and elevated white cell count. What is the most important management? [cite: 3228, 3229, 3230, 3231, 3232]
options: B- Aspiration of knee and injection with steroid [cite: 3234]
D- Commence oral antibiotics and discharge [cite: 3236]
E- Aspiration of knee and send fluid for M, C+ [cite: 3237]
questions.explanation: This history is indicative of septic arthritis and this must be excluded therefore it is essential to send the effusion for microbiological analysis. [cite: 5382]

questions.question: A 22 year old male presents with a swollen right knee. A few weeks earlier he had had bloody diarrhoea thought to be secondary to salmonella. He is otherwise well. On examination there is a large effusion of his right knee. How would you manage this patient? [cite: 3238, 3239, 3240, 3241]
options: A-Exclude a septic arthritis then intra articular steroid injection [cite: 3242]
questions.explanation: The right knee effusion given the history of salmonella food poisoning is likely a reactive arthritis. When troublesome intra articular steroids are useful however samples should be sent to exclude a septic arthritis. [cite: 5384, 5385]

questions.question: A 24 year old male has recently had unprotected sex. He presents with arthritis, red watery eyes and dysuria. He also has noticed plaques on his hands. What is the most likely diagnosis? [cite: 3247, 3248, 3249]
questions.explanation: The triad of arthritis, conjunctivitis and urethritis are classically of Reiters syndrome. It commonly occurs after chlamydia and infective diarrhoea such as salmonella or shigella.It is associated with B27. Keratoderma blennorrhagica is a feature in Reiters syndrome where plaques are evident on the soles and palms. Balanitis circinata can also occur where there are lesions evident on the penis. [cite: 5387, 5388, 5389, 5390]

questions.question: In a DEXA scan, how should a Z-score of 0 and a T-score of-0.8 be interpreted? [cite: 3256]
questions.explanation: The T-score is the BMD measurement compared to that of the average person at their peak bone mass. The Z-score is the BMD score compared to the normal adjusted for age.A Z-score of O means that the individual has a normal BMD for their age. [cite: 5392, 5393]

questions.question: A 34 year old female with SLE has severe renal involvement and is being treated with IV cyclophosphamide. She presents very unwell with pyrexia, cough and shortness of breath. She is found to be pancytopenic and her saturations are only 88% following a short walk. Her Chest X-ray shows diffuse reticular opacification. What is the most likely diagnosis? [cite: 3262, 3263, 3264, 3265, 3266]
questions.explanation: The X-ray findings and the fact this patient is immunosuppressed and has pancytopenia makes the most likely diagnosis pneumocystis jiroveci. It leads to exercised induced hypoxia. [cite: 5395, 5396]

questions.question: In a patient with SLE who suffers from arthralgia and mouth ulcers, but no other organ involvement, how would you manage them? [cite: 3272, 3273]
questions.explanation: If only the joints are affected and no other serious systemic involvement hydroxychloroquine is useful. [cite: 5398]

questions.question: A 29 year old presents with a DVT. She has a previous history of SLE and recurrent miscarriages. Bloods reveal a prolonged APTR and low platelets. What is the most likely diagnosis? [cite: 3279, 3280, 3281]
questions.explanation: The antiphospholipid antibody syndrome is characterized by thrombocytopenia, recurrent thromboses and recurrent miscarriage. Anticardiolipin antibodies are found to be positive. Livedo reticularis can be a feature. The antiphospholipid syndrome can be primary when on its own or secondary if SLE is evident. Factor V Leiden and Prothrombin mutation can lead to thromboses but not usually recurrent miscarriages. [cite: 5400, 5401, 5402]

questions.question: A 35 year old with a known history of rheumatoid arthritis on prednisolone and hydroxychloroquine, presents with pyrexia and a LRTI. Bloods reveal a WCC of 7.0 with neutrophils of 6.0 and a raised CRFP and ESR. How should you manage this patient? [cite: 3288, 3289, 3290]
options: A- Antibiotics and increase dose of prednisolone [cite: 3291]
questions.explanation: In a patient on long term steroids who has infective symptoms then steroids should be doubled and the infection treated. DMARDs should only be stopped if there is pancytopenia. [cite: 5404, 5405]

questions.question: A 28 year old presents with a facial rash, joint pain and fever. There is no evidence of active synovitis and there is a malar butterfly rash over her nose and cheeks. Anti-dsDNA and anti-Ro antibodies are positive. What is the most likely diagnosis? [cite: 3296, 3297, 3298, 3299]
questions.explanation: SLE is the most likely diagnosis given the history of arthritis with relatively normal joints and the malar butterfly rash. Antibodies against dsDNA and Ro are highly indicative. [cite: 5408, 5409]

questions.question: If a man is planning to start a family then what drug is safest in managing his rheumatoid arthritis? [cite: 3305, 3306]
questions.explanation: Prednisolone is the safest. Sulfasalazine leads to transient aspermia and the rest are teratogenic. [cite: 5411, 5412]

questions.question: A 73 year old female has a long history of Rheumatoid Arthritis on methotrexate and hydroxychloroquine. However recently he has noticed peripheral oedema and swelling around his eyes. Urinalysis reveals protein and a 24 urine collection is suspected. You suspected nephrotic syndrome. What is the most likely diagnosis? [cite: 3312, 3313, 3314, 3315]
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is Amyloidosis due to the long history. Gold and penicillamine classically lead to nephrotic syndrome. NSAID nephropathy usually does not lead to a nephrotic syndrome. [cite: 5414, 5415]

questions.question: A 62 year old female presents with pain and stiffness of the joints around the pelvic girdle and shoulders and neck. Her morning stiffness in these areas lasts for approximately 2 hours. She is also complaining of scalp tenderness. She is also fatigued. Bloods reveal a normochromic normocytic anaemia and a raised ESR. Rheumatoid factor is negative. She has a mild pyrexia. What is the most likely diagnosis? [cite: 3321, 3322, 3323, 3324, 3325]
questions.explanation: PMR presents with hip and shoulder girdle pain and stiffness and fatigue. Immune complexes can be evident. Synovitis can occur in PMR usually in the knees. ESR is raised and can be used to monitor the disease. It can be associated with temporal arteritis. Polymyositis presents with proximal muscle weakness as does dermatomyositis however with a characteristic rash. [cite: 5417, 5418, 5419]

questions.question: A 58 year old male presents with pain in his MCPs bilaterally, his ankles, wrists and knees. He is stiff for 3 hours in the morning. He has lost some weight. Bloods reveal raised inflammatory markers and a normochromic, normocytic anaemia. Rheumatoid factor and ANA are negative and a CK is 175. Which of of the following is the most likely diagnosis? [cite: 3331, 3332, 3333, 3334, 3335]
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is RA. SLE could lead to these symptoms but autoantibodies would be positive and joints are normal. PMR does not show this joint involvement pattern. [cite: 5421, 5422]

questions.question: A 63 year old man with a history of hypertension is on bendroflumethiazide. He presents with an acutely swollen and very painful big toe. How would you reliably distinguish gout from a septic arthritis as the cause? [cite: 3342, 3343, 3344]
options: D- Negatively birefringent crystals in synovial fluid [cite: 3348]
questions.explanation: The only way to reliably distinguish gout from a septic arthritis is the presence of negatively birefringent crystals in the synovial fluid. [cite: 5424, 5425]

questions.question: A 65 year old female presents a painful right knee. An x-ray of the knee shows linear calcification of the articular cartilage and lateral meniscus. Given the likely diagnosis, what would you find on aspiration of the joint? [cite: 3350, 3351, 3352]
questions.explanation: The patient has pseudogout and the diagnosis is based on the finding of weakly positive birefringent calcium pyrophosphate crystals in synovial fluid. [cite: 5427]

questions.question: A 40 year old female presents with weakness. She has difficulty getting up from the chair and when climbing stairs. She is also fatigued, noticed weight loss and feeling fevered. On examination there is wasting of the pelvic girdle muscles and power is $4/5$ Anti Jo-l antibodies are positive. What is the most likely diagnosis? [cite: 3358, 3359, 3360, 3361]
questions.explanation: The history and clinical findings are indicative of polymyositis. It leads to progressive proximal muscle weakness. There may be wasting of the muscles. In severe cases the respiratory muscles are involved. The EMG shows a typical triad of spontaneous fibrillation potentials at rest; polyphasic or short-duration potentials on voluntary contraction; and repetitive potentials on mechanical stimulation of the nerve. [cite: 5429, 5430, 5431, 5432, 5433, 5434]

questions.question: A 12 year old boy known to have haemophilia presents with a painful swollen right knee. The movement of the knee is severely restricted by pain. Inflammatory markers are normal and rheumatoid factor is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis? [cite: 3368, 3369, 3370]
questions.explanation: This patient due to his previous history is likely to have bled into his knee. Septic arthritis should be ruled out and you would expect a raise in the inflammatory markers. JIA is less likely given the past history. At 12 the patient is too young for osteoarthritis and gout [cite: 5436, 5437, 5438]

questions.question: A 25 year old gentleman has recently returned from travelling abroad. He presents with a red eye and a swollen knee and ankle. He states he did have unprotected sex whilst travelling. What further investigation is required for the diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is a reactive arthritis secondary to an STI. The diagnosis is made from the history and examination findings. The symptoms can occur up to 6 weeks following a Gl or genitourinary infection. It leads to an acute, asymmetrical, lower limb arthritis. All cultures from joint and blood are negative but it is important septic arthritis is excluded.

questions.question: A 69 year old female with a previous history of rheumatoid arthritis, currently on methotrexate, presents with painful, swelling of her right knee. She is also pyrexial and generally unwell. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The diagnosis you should worry about in this case is a septic arthritis given the sudden onset and the fact she is generally unwell. Methotrexate can lead to bone marrow suppression and thus lead to increased risk of infections. Pseudogout and gout can lead to swelling however pseudogout does not cause fever and gout is less likely due to the joint involved. Similarly osteoarthritis does not lead to fever and malaise. A flair of rheumatoid arthritis is obviously a possibility however the joint involved and fever and malaise mean that septic arthritis should first be suspected.

questions.question: A 22 year old female presents with a facial rash, fever and malaise. She is also complaining of painful joints in her wrists and fingers. What is most likely to be found in her bloods.
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is systemic lupus erythematosus. It is much more common in females with a ration of approximately 9:1 to men and most often occurs in the early 20s. This is an autoimmune disease and thus leads to immune complex deposition and thus complement levels are always low in active disease and therefore this is the most likely blood result finding. Anti dsDNA can be evident about 50% however is more likely to be positive in those with severe systemic involvement. RF is only found in about a quarter of cases.

questions.question: A 60 year old gentleman with a history of recurrent rhinitis and otitis media, presents with increasing shortness of breath on exertion. A CXR reveal multiple nodules throughout the lungs and a dipstick of his urine reveals a microscopic haematuria and proteinuria. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Wegeners granulomatosis is the most likely diagnosis. It is a vasculitis which commonly afiects the upper respiratory tract and renal and pulmonary systems. There is often a history of rhinorrhoea and sinusitis and pulmonary features such as cough and shortness of breath, and arthralgia. It can lead to nodular lung disease and renal involvement which can lead to a glomerulonephritis thus the haematuria and proteinuria seen here. Goodpastures syndrome often leads to renal disease and can also lead to haemoptysis but not the other features described in the history. SLE and RA would not account for all of these mans symptoms.

questions.question: What blood test would be most useful in the diagnosis of limited cutaneous scleroderma?
questions.explanation: In about 80% of cases of limited cutaneous scleroderma there is evidence of anticentromere antibodies. RF and ANA are present in about one third but are not specific. Anti smooth muscle antibodies are useful for autoimmune hepatitis and anti Ro for the diagnosis of Sjögrens

questions.question: A 65 year old woman is recovering in hospital following a knee replacement. She is known to have a history of alcohol excess and has had previously a duodenal ulcer for which she is on omeprazole. What would you prescribe for prophylaxsis for a DVT while she is post op.
options: C- Subcutaneous low molecular weight heparin
E-Nil due to risk of bleeding
questions.explanation: LMWH should be used for all prophylaxsis of DVTs due to its efficacy, ease of administration and it does not require monitoring unlike IV heparin. Although it can not be as easily

questions.question: A 64 year old gentleman who is known to drink alcohol excessively presents with a red, hot swollen ankle. What investigation should be performed for a definitive diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis here is gout due to the history and known alcohol excess. Joint aspiration and microscopy may show negatively birefringent crystal which are needle.shaped. Serum urate levels are useful however they can be low in acute attacks of gout.

questions.question: An 80 year old male presents with a painful hip and knee. He is known to have a peptic ulcer and is on omeprazole. He has limited internal rotation of the hip. What analgesia do you prescribe initially?
questions.explanation: This gentleman is most likely to be suffering from osteoarthritis. Paracetamol should be used in this case according to the analgesic ladder. NSAIDs are not appropriate in this case due to the peptic ulcer disease.

questions.question: An 19 year old male presents with back pain and morning stiffness. It is relieved with exercise. An X-ray was performed of his lumbar spine and showed obliteration of the sacroiliac junction. What treatment is the most appropriate?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is ankylosing spondylitis. NSAIDs and regular physiotherapy are the most useful in the management od ihis patient. Bed rest and cortisol injections are not useful.

questions.question: A 68 year old female has had pain in her left knee for numerous years. She is now waking up in the middle of the night with the pain and her knee is giving way and she has fallen several times. The knee is unstable on examination There is evidence of Herberdens and Bouchards nodes on the hands. How would you manage this patient?
questions.explanation: This patient clearly has severe osteoarthritis of the knee with significant symptoms and instability. A knee replacement is thus indicated.

questions.question: A 4 year old girl is complaining of pain in her thigh and hip. On examination she is tender on palpation of the thigh. Her bloods show elevated inflammatory markers. An ultrasound and x-ray of the hip and femur is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The most likely is osteomyelitis as the pain is in the thigh. It is unlikely to be a fracture or bone tumor due to the normal x-ray, However osteomyelitis does not show up on the x-ray initially and then later it can show haziness and loss of density of the bone, then followed by subperiosteal reaction and sequestrum. Septic arthritis is unlikely as the joint is normal. Perthes disease is osteochondritis of the epiphysis of the femoral head and there would normally be x-ray findings with the earliest being widening of the joint space, followed by loss of the nuclear femoral head with patchy density. It does not cause raised inflammatory markers.

questions.question: A 13 year old boy is complaining of left hip pain. On examination, internal rotation of the hip is very limited. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Slipped upper femoral epiphysis is the most likely diagnosis. It normally affects children between 10 and 16. It is associated with obesity and hypogonadism. There is limited internal rotation and adduction of the hip. Perthes disease is osteochondritis of the femoral head and typically affects a younger age group those between 3 and 11. On examination unlike SUFE there is limited movement in all directions. The history and clinical findings are not indicative of the other diagnoses.

questions.question: A 3 year old girl is generally unwell and pyrexial. She is also unable to weight bear due to hip pain. Her inflammatory markers are markedly raised. An X-ray shows a widened joint space. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis here is septic arthritis due to the history and raised jnflammatory markers. An early feature on x-ray is a widened joint space. Osteomyelitis is less likely due to the pain being in the joint, the sudden onset and how unwell the patient is. The other diagnosis do not cause the patient to be pyrexial or unwell. Perthes disease is osteochondritis of the femoral head, affecting children aged between 3 and ||years. It presents with pain in the hip or knee and causes a limp.

questions.question: A9 year old boy is complaining of hip and groin pain. On examination he walks with a limp and there is limited restriction of all movements of the joint. An x-ray reveals flattening of the femoral head. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Perthes disease is the most likely diagnosis due to the history, the restriction of all hip joint movements and the x-ray findings. It begins with widened joint space and then reduced density and flattened femoral head and the further deformity. The patient is too well for this to be a septic arthritis. SUFE affects older children and predominantly internal rotation and adduction.

questions.question: A 32 year old female presents with painful wrists and hands. Her wrists and hands are very stifrin the morning and only loosen off after 2 hours. On examination there is active synovitis in both wrists and over several PIPs and MCPs. What test is useful in aiding the diagnosis?
options: C- X-ray if hands and wrists
questions.explanation: The history is very indicative of Rheumatoid arthritis and Rheumatoid factor is positive in about three quarters of all patients. X-rays are useful in monitoring for erosions as the disease progresses and in guiding therapy however is unlikely to show significant changes indicative of RA at this early stage.

questions.question: A 55 year old female presents with knee pain. She has problems for sometime with pain in her DIPs and the base of her thumb. On examination there is pain on the medial aspect of the knee joint and there is evidence of Bouchard and Herberdens nodes. She is liff in the morning however the pain worsens in the evening and after movement. She has a family history of osteoarthritis. What investigation will give the definitive diagnosis?
questions.explanation: This woman most likely has nodal generalized osteoarthritis. This is a subset which leads to multiple joint involvement of OA, which can be severe and sudden onset, predominantly the knee hips and hands with Bouchard and Heberdens nodes. It is thought to be an autoimmune disease and a synovial membrane biopsy would show immune complex deposition.

questions.question: A 45 year old woman with a 10 year history of Rheumatoid Arthritis develops suddenly a painful, hot, swollen, tender knee with very restricted movement. How would you investigate?
options: C- Joint fluid aspiration for crystal examination
D- Joint fluid aspirate for microscopy and culture
questions.explanation: Despite the history of Rheumatoid arthritis, this history should always raise suspicion of a septic arthritis and therefore joint aspiration for microscopy and culture should be performed.

questions.question: A patient with SLE presents with deteriorating vision over the last few months. On examination there is no evidence of redness in the sclera however it is difficult to perform opthalmoscopy due to opacities in the lenses of the eyes. Given the likely diagnosis, how you manage this?
options: D- Advise her to visit the optician
E- Referral for extracapsular lens extraction
questions.explanation: This patient has cataracts, which can occur at an earlier age in systemic lupus erythematosus and thus she should be referred to an ophthalmologist for surgical removal of the lens.

questions.question: A 64 year old gentleman presents with a left sided headache which is severe. He has noticed his scalp is very tender when brushing his hair. What treatment is required to ensure no vision loss occurs?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is temporal arteritis which can lead to sudden vision loss. A high dose of oral steroids is required to reduce the risk of visual loss. Intravenous steroids are utilized if there is vision loss in one eye to try to avoid vision loss in the other eye.

questions.question: A 60 year old female presents with hip and shoulder girdle pain. She is generally lethargic and is stiff in the morning. She states she can barely brush her hair due to pain in her upper arm. She has an elevated ESR. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is Polymyalgia rheumatica as the history and high ESR is very indicative of this. In polymyositis there is symmetrical proximal muscle weakness and an EMG shows; spontaneous fibrillation potentials at rest; polyphasic or short duration potentials on voluntary contraction; and salvos of repetitive potentials on mechanical Stimulation of the nerve. Dermatomyositis presents in a similar fashion however there is characteristic skin changes such as heliotropic rash around eyes or Gottrons papules. Fibromyalgia results in generalized aches and pains with certain trigger points and the ESR is normal.

questions.question: A 28 year old woman presents to her GP with general aches and pains. She is generally fatigued. On examination there is nothing specific to find however there is certain points when pushed which elicit pain. Her bloods are normal. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis here is fibromyalgia due to the non-specific history and normal examination and blood results

questions.question: A 42 year old gentleman presents with difficulty climbing stairs and combing his hair. He is suffering from general malaise and is feeling feverish. On examination there is a proximal muscle weakness, a purplish rash around his eyelids and papules over his knuckles. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The diagnosis is dermatomyositis due to the proximal muscle weakness and the characteristic skin changes.

questions.question: A 15 year old female is brought to the GP as her parents have noticed she has a poor posture with rounded shoulders and a humped back. On examination there is severe kyphosis of the thoracic area. Given the likely diagnosis, what would you not expect to see on a thoracic Xray?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is Scheurmanns disease. This is an osteochondroses and it affects the normal ossification of ring epiphyses of thoracic vertebrae. It affects typically girls aged 13 to 16. It leads to wedge shaped vertebrae and thus kyphosis. Other features on Xray is narrow intervertebral spaces, Schmorls node (which are herniations of nucleus pulposus of vertebral plates) and irregular end plates.

questions.question: A 32 year old gentleman presents to A+E following a back injury. He is suffering from numbness, paraesthesia and weakness of the leg and has been unable to pass urine. On examination there is loss of peri anal sensation and it confirms reduced power and numbness in the left leg. What is your next course of action?
questions.explanation: The diagnosis here is cauda equina syndrome. An urgent neurosurgical referral for surgical intervention is required.

questions.question: A 22 year old male who plays many sports regularly complains of intermittent swelling of his knee and locking. He suffers from knee pain after exercising. Arthroscopy is performed and shows several loose bodies in the synovial cavity. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Osteochondritis dissecans is the most likely diagnosis. It leads to local necrosis of the articular cartilage and underlying bone which leads to the formation of a loose body. The knee is commonly affected especially the medial femoral condyle. Osteoarthritis is unlikely at this age. An ACKL rupture leads to a haemarthrosis. A meniscal tear can occur but does not lead to the arthroscopy findings.

questions.question: When managing polymyositis and dermatomyositis, what blood test can be utilized for monitoring the result?
questions.explanation: The most beneficial blood test to monitor the response to treatment and activity of the disease is CK. The other blood results may be raised in some cases of polymyositis and dermatomyositis however are not raised in all cases and are therefore less useful.

questions.question: A 70 year old female presents with sudden onset swollen and painful knee. She is generally unwell with a fever. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is septic arthritis and in any patient with this history then a septic joint is presumed until proven otherwise. Gout can present similarly however is not associated with fever and malaise.

questions.question: A 20 year old male presents with pain and stiffness in his lumbar spine relived by exercise. He is positive for HLA B27 gene. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The history and age of the patient is very indicative of ankylosing spondylitis. In the majority of patients the HLA B27 gene is present. The other diagnoses do not fit with the history given.

questions.question: A 25 year old gentleman presents to his GP with pains in his left knee and ankles. He is also suffering from dysuria and red eye. He has noticed plaques on the palms of his hands and soles of his feet and a rash on his glans penis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Reiters syndrome is the triad of arthritis, urethritis and conjunctivitis. It can be associated with keratoderma blennorrhagic which are psoriatic like lesions. It most often follows chlamydia or Gl infections such as with shigella, campylobacter and salmonella Reactive arthritis can lead to an asymmetrical lower limb arthritis also but not the other features. The other diagnoses are much less likely.

questions.question: A 67 year old present with severe thoracic back pain. His bloods revealed renal impairment and an xray shows osteolytic lesions in his vertebrae. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is multiple myeloma, plasma cell neoplasm. It leads to bone marrow infiltration and localised osteolytic deposits. It also leads to paraprotein bands and Bence Jones proteins which can lead to renal impairment. Pagets disease leads to areas of bone growth and resorption. Prostate cancer can lead to osteolytic and osteoblastic lesions and there is often other associated symptoms such as hesitancy etc. Osteoporosis does not explain the features.

questions.question: A 45 year old female has noticed arm weakness. She has noticed hat she has found it increasingly difficult to brush her hair, lift objects and climb stairs. On examination there is evidence of reduced power in her proximal muscles and wasting and bloods reveal an elevated CK. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The history and clinical findings are indicative of polymyositis. Dysphagia and dysphonia can develop. Distal muscles are spared. Polymyalgia rheumatica presents with pain and stiffness of the hip and shoulder girdles and proximal muscles unlike Polymyositis where pain is not a common feature. The history is not indicative of myasthenia gravis or fibromyalgia and CK is elevated.

questions.question: A patient with psoriasis develops swelling and pain in the joints of her hands. On examination there is swelling and tenderness in the DIPs. What treatment is most useful?
questions.explanation: This patient has developed psoriatic arthritis and methotrexate is utilized as it can lead to major deformities. It must be closely monitored.

questions.question: A 42 year old farmer presents with arthralgia and myalgia, malaise and intermittent fever. There is evidence of lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly. Given the likely diagnosis, what treatment should be utilized ?
options: B- Doxycycline and rifampicin and gentamicin
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is brucellosis as it is common in farm workers. The drug combination which leads to lowest risk of relapse is triple therapy with doxycycline, rifampicin and gentamicin. Co-trimoxazole can be utilized for an oral alternative.

questions.question: A 60 year old female from Asia presents complaining of pain in her bones and muscle weakness. An xray is performed of the femur and reveals linear low density areas surrounded by sclerotic areas. Bloods revealed elevated ALP, low phosphate and normal calcium levels. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The diagnosis is osteomalacia with the characteristic evidence of Loosers zones on the x-s ray. It leads to elevated ALP and low phosphate due to parathroid hormone excretion. In Pagets disease the ALP is also elevated however calcium and phosphate levels are normal. However unlike osteomalacia there is evidence on x-ray of sclerotic phase of bone expansion and loss of distinction between cortex and trabeculae. Osteoporosis does hot lead to the x-ray or blood results and only causes pain when there has been a fracture. Similarly hyperparathyroidism and renal osteodystrophy do not lead to the features described.

questions.question: A 63 year old female is found to have a pathological fracture of her femur. An Xray showed patchy sclerosis, thickening of the trabeculae and loss of distinction between the trabeculae and cortex. What treatment should be initiated?
options: C- Calcium and vitamin D supplements
questions.explanation: The diagnosis is Paget's disease and bisphosphonates should be utilized. They are analogues of bone pyrophosphate and adhere to hydroxyapatite and aims to inhibit osteoclasts.

questions.question: A 50 year old male presents with bone pain and lower back pain. On examination there is evidence of kyphosis, frontal bossing of the skull and deafness. What do you expect to find in blood results?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is Pagets disease due to the typical deformities and deafness due to expansion of skull and compression of cranial nerve VIII. It can have an autosomal dominant inheritance. ALP is elevated in this condition.

questions.question: A 40 year old man presents with arthralgia. He also gives a history of steatorrhoea and abdominal pain. A biopsy of the small bowel reveals stunted villi with PAS positive macrophages. What is characteristic of this disease?
options: E- Bacilli within macrophages on electron microscopy
questions.explanation: The diagnosis is likely to be Whipples disease. And as well as PAS positive macrophages there is evidence of bacilli within macrophages. The rest of the options are not specific features.

questions.question: A 24 year old known to have chlamydia presents with swelling in her knee and ankle. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is reactive arthritis secondary to Chlamydia trachomatis. Reiters syndrome is the triad of arthritis, conjunctivitis and urethritis and often there is characteristic skin changes. The other options are much less likely.

questions.question: A 20 year old with back pain which is relieved with exercise and is associated with morning stiffness. An X-ray shows obscuring of the sacroiliac joints. Which of the following treatments is helpful?
options: B- Physiotherapy and Spinal extension exercises
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is ankylosing spondylitis. The treatment includes NSAIDs and spinal extension exercises and regular physiotherapy. Spinal osteotomy is rarely used for severe deformity. The other options are not useful.

questions.question: What is the most characteristic finding on Xray of a patient with ankylosing spondylitis?
options: A- Subchondral bony sclerosis at sacroiliac joints
questions.explanation: The characteristic early x-ray findings is subchondral bony sclerosis on the iliac sides of the sacroiliac joints. It eventually leads on to bamboo spine. The other options are not characteristic.

questions.question: What would you expect to find in the blood results of a patient with osteoporosis?
options: D- Normal calcium, phosphate and ALP levels
questions.explanation: The blood results are typically normal for calcium, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase, vitamin D.

questions.question: A 22 year old who has recently recovered from an episode of shigella gastroenteritis, presents with pain and swelling of his left knee and ankle. He also has noticed red eyes and a rash on his glans penis and plaques on his palms and soles. What other feature if present is highly indicative of Reiters Syndrome
questions.explanation: Keratoderma blenorrhagica which are brown yellow waxy lesions on the soles and palms are highly indicative of Reiters Syndrome.

questions.question: A 62 year old female with known osteoarthritis and diabetes presents with sudden swelling and pain in her left knee. It is hot, red and tender. What investigation should be performed?
options: C- Joint aspiration for gram stain, microscopy and culture
questions.explanation: With this history septic arthritis should be at the top of the differential diagnosis and therefore joint aspiration for gram stain, microscopy and culture is essential. An x-ray is not diagnostic. Fluid microscopy on its own is only useful for diagnosis of gout and pseudogout. The history could make gout a possible diagnosis however a septic arthritis must always be excluded. Patients are usually systemically unwell and pyrexial in septic arthritis.

questions.question: A 32 year old female with psoriasis presents with painful swollen fingers with some deformity. What is the most appropriate treatment?
questions.explanation: This lady is presenting with psoriatic arthritis. Methotrexate or ciclosporin can be utilized in severe disease. Etanercept is also very useful but should only be utilized once methotrexate or ciclosporin fail. Sulfasalazine can be utilized in more mild disease,

questions.question: What HLA type is most associated with SLE?
questions.explanation: There is an increased frequency of systemic lupus erythematosus in those with HLA.B8 and -DR3

questions.question: What blood result abnormality is included in the ACR diagnostic criteria for polyarteritis nodosa?
questions.explanation: The blood results included in the diagnostic criteria are elevated urea and creatinine and Hep. B infection.

questions.question: How do you monitor the response of Giant cell arteritis to treatment?
options: C- Positive to negative temporal artery biopsy
questions.explanation: ESR is useful for monitoring the response to treatment. A biopsy is not utilized to monitor response as although a positive biopsy confirms the diagnosis, it may be negative due to skip lesions and thus is not utilized.

questions.question: A 60 year old female presents with pain and stiffiness of the shoulder, neck and hips. She is stiff for up to one hour in the morning. Her ESR is elevated. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The symptoms are indicative of PMR. Polymyositis leads to symmetrical proximal muscle weakness but pain is unusual. Frozen shoulder restricts all movements of the shoulders. The joints involved are not typical of Rheumatoid arthritis.

questions.question: A patient with rheumatoid arthritis for numerous years present with shortness of breath, mouth ulcers and malaise Bloods reveal a pancytopenia. What medications is likely to be the cause?
questions.explanation: Gold is the only option which can lead to pulmonary fibrosis, pancytopenia and mouth ulceration.

questions.question: What would you find in a patients blood results who is suffering from Feltys Syndrome?
questions.explanation: Feltys syndrome is whereby RA is associated with splenomegaly and this leads to normocytic normochromic anaemia or hypochromic anaemia with neutropenia or pancytopenia may occur.

questions.question: Which of the following feature is most indicative of an inflammatory arthritis?
options: A- Morning stiffness for more than an half an hour
questions.explanation: The most indicative feature of an inflammatory arthritis is morning stiffness.

questions.question: What deformity in Rheumatoid arthritis is likely to cause a finger drop?
options: D- Swelling and dorsal subluxation of the ulnar styloid
questions.explanation: Swelling and dorsal subluxation of the ulnar styloid can lead to rupture of the extensor tendons and thus can lead to finger drop. The other deformities are seen in RA however do not lead to finger drop.

questions.question: In rheumatoid arthritis, what would you expect the synovial membrane to look like?
options: B- Vascular proliferation on the synovial membrane
E- Normal membrane but viscous fluid
questions.explanation: In RA, the synovial membrane shows marked vascular proliferation with increased permeability of blood vessels. Thickening of the membrane may also be seen. The viscosity of fluid is decreased.

questions.question: Which feature in the history of someone with Osteoarthritis aids in deciding the best course of management?
options: E- History of severe pain and stiffness in the knees
questions.explanation: The management of the patient should be guided with the history and severity of the symptoms.

questions.question: A 68 year old male presents with leg pain on walking. His leg feel heavy and sometimes numb. It is worse walking down hill and is relieved when he stops and sits down. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis given is spinal stenosis. It is caused by narrowing of the spinal canal causing root ischaemia and neurogenic claudication. It is often caused by a Combination of loss of disc space, osteophyte formation and a hypertrophic ligamentum flavum. There can be reduction of spinal diameter due to osteoarthritis. An x-ray is normal and straight leg raising test is negative. It is often exacerbated by extension of the spine and thus going downhill can be worse and when sitting down. This is the main differentiating feature from its main differential Intermittent claudication where these features are not seen.

questions.question: A 72 year old male has been suffering from neck pain for a number of years. He is now complaining of worsened pain and his left arm feeling weak and numb. On examination he has sensory loss in C5 and C6 dermatomes and he has 4/5 power in left shoulder abduction. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The diagnosis is prolapsed disc C5 C6 due to the history and clinical findings. Cervical spondylosis occurs secondary to osteoarthritis. Disc spaces are sometimes narrowed and osteophytes can impinge on the nerve but there is usually no muscle weakness.

questions.question: A 72 year old male with cervical spondylosis presents with pain and weakness in both arms. He has also noticed them feeling numb and tingling. On examination there is evidence of LMN signs in his arms and UMN signs in his legs. How would you manage this patient?
options: C- Urgent CT of Head and Neck
questions.explanation: This gentleman must be urgently referred to the neurosurgeons as there are features of a central disc prolapse and cord compression.

questions.question: A 37 year old female twisted her ankle a few weeks earlier. Since then she has had pain in her foot. She describes this as burning and is sometimes tingling. The symptoms are reproduced by pressing behind the medial malleolus. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: This patient is suffering from tarsal tunnel syndrome which is due to compression of the posterior tibial nerve. In common peroneal nerve injury there is foot drop and sensory loss is over the front and lateral half of the leg and dorsum of the foot.

questions.question: A patient with rheumatoid arthritis is complaining of pain her left hand which is worse in the morning and sometimes wakes her from sleep. She also feels her hand is numb. On examination there is loss of sensation in her left thumb index, middle and radial half of ring finger. What clinical feature may you also observe?
options: D- Weakness and wasting of the muscles of the thenar eminence
E- Pain relieved if the wrist is hyperfelexed
questions.explanation: The diagnosis is carpal tnnel syndrome and the only option which is also a feature is weakness and wasting of the thenar muscles.

questions.question: A 23 year old female presents with a discoid rash. She is also complaining of painful joints and has noticed her skin being very sensitive in the sun. She has also noticed an increased frequency of oral ulcers. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is systemic lupus erythematosus given the history and findings. The history is not indicative of any of the of the other diagnoses. There is specific criteria for the diagnosis of SLE.

questions.question: A 23 year old female presents with a discoid rash, photosensitivity and painful joints. She has also noticed an increased frequency of oral ulcers. There is also evidence of microscopic haematuria and proteinuria. What antibody is specific to the diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The diagnosis is SLE and anti dsDNA antibody levels are specific for this. Anti centromere is more specific for scleroderma. Anti smooth muscle antibody is seen in autoimmune hepatitis.

questions.question: A 65 year old presents with headache. He is also feeling feverish and generally unwell. He has also noticed his scalp is sensitive when he brushes his hair and is having pain when chewing. What treatment should you initiate?
questions.explanation: The history is indicative of giant-cell arteritis and thus oral steroids must be initiated. IV steroids are only utilized if there is sudden vision loss to ensure there is no loss of vision in other eye. Obviously a rheumatology referral will be required however this should not delay the initiation of steroids which must be commenced immediately.

questions.question: A 65 year old presents with headache. He is also feeling feverish and generally unwell. He has also noticed his scalp is sensitive when he brushes his hair and is having pain when chewing. What will make the definitive diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The definitive diagnosis is via a temporal artery biopsy. However there can be skip lesions and a negative biopsy does not exclude the diagnosis.

questions.question: A 63 year old female is complaining of pain around her shoulders and hip. She is very stiff in the morning. She is feeling fatigued. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is PMR given the pain and morning stiffness around the shoulder and hip girdle. There is also proximal muscle pain and these can be tender on palpation. There can be significant systemic features such as malaise, pyrexia, depression and night sweats, anorexia and weight loss. Rheumatoid arthritis does not typically effect these

questions.question: A 19 year old male presents generally unwell, feeling feverish. He has noticed a salmon pink, maculopapular rash on his trunk and arms. He is complaining of joint pain with painful and swollen distal interphalangeal joints are swollen. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is adult-onset Stills disease. It affects [predominantly the age group 15 to 35. It usually present with a salmon pink maculo papular rash, pyrexia (typically in the evening) and arthritis (which can be worsened during the pyrexial period). The rash is usually on the trunks and legs but can be on face and arms and usually appears during pyrexia. A sore throat can also be a feature, as can hepatosplenomegaly, generalised lymphadenopathy, and polyserositis including pericarditis and pleuritis. The other options do not explain all of the symptoms oints.

questions.question: A 33 year old gentleman has noticed recurrent mouth and genital ulcers. He is also suffering from diarrhoea intermittently and has complained of red eyes. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis to explain all of these symptoms is Behcets disease. It is presumed to be autoimmune and can effect multiple organ systems. The diagnosis do not account for all of the symptoms. SLE can lead to mouth ulcers but not genital. Lichen planus and Pemphigus are not associated with red eye or diarrhoea.

questions.question: A 45 year old patient with a raised BMI presents with a hot, swollen, red very painful big toe. How do you manage this?
questions.explanation: This patient has presented with gout and non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug are very useful. Allopurinol should be used prophylactically but should not be started during an acute attack. Steroids may be useful where NSAIDs are absolutely contraindicated.

questions.question: A 45 year old patient with a raised BMI presents with a hot, swollen, red very painful big toe. What investigation would give the definitive diagnosis?
options: B- Joint fluid aspiration for microscopy
questions.explanation: This patient has most likely gout. Although urate levels can be high they can also be low during an acute attack. Fluid aspiration for microscopy which reveals negatively birefringent crystals.

questions.question: A 45 year old patient with a raised BMI presents with a hot, swollen, red very painful big toe. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Gout is the most likely diagnosis given the acuteness and clinical findings and the joint involved. The first MTP is often the most common joint to be affected. Although other joints such as knees, ankles and wrists can be involved. It is excruciating pain and very tender and can wake the patient from sleep. Due to the severe inflammatory response it can lead to malaise and pyrexia. It leads to hot tender and erythematous joints which when resolving the skin can desquamate and be pruritic. Pseudogout usually is associated with other disease such as OA and most commonly affects the knees and ankles. If there is any suspicion of septic arthritis then this must be excluded.

questions.question: A 13 year old boy presents to is GP. HE has been generally unwell with a fever for approximately one week. On examination there is evidence of bilateral conjunctivitis, cervical lymphadenopathy, erythema and desquamation and oedema of his hands and feet and his lips appear red and dry. Given the likely diagnosis, what treatment should be given?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is Kawasakis. This can lead to effects on the cardiovascular system and other systems. Aspirin and intravenous immunoglobulin used in conjunction lead to a lower incidence of coronary artery abnormalities. The treatment should begin within the first ten days.

questions.question: A 13 year old boy presents to is GP. He has been generally unwell with a fever for approximately one week. On examination there is evidence of bilateral conjunctivitis, cervical lymphadenopathy, erythema and desquamation and oedema of his hands and feet and his lips appear red and dry. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The diagnosis is Kawasakis Disease. The diagnosis is based on the criteria of: pyrexia greater than 5 days, bilateral conjunctivitis, dryness, redness and fissuring of mouth and lips (strawberry tongue), cervical lymphadneopathy, erythema, desquamation and oedema of palms and soles and a polymorphic rash. The other options do not account for all clinical features.

questions.question: A 72 year old female who is overweight presents with pains in her fingers. She has also noticed some pain in her knees. These are worst after movement and at the end of the day. On examination there is nil of note on knee examination and there is evidence of hard swelling at the PIPs and DIPs. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is OA. This is indicated by the history with pain worst after movement and at the end of the day. There is also evidence of Bouchards and Heberdens nodes. There may be some effusion in affected joints and crepitus. RA differs in that the pain is worst in the morning and there is morning stiffness.

questions.question: A 42 year old female presents with dry, gritty eyes and a dry mouth. She is feeling tired and is having some difficulty swallowing. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is Sjögrens syndrome where there is inflammation and the destruction of exocrine glands. It predominantly affects the salivary and lacrimal glands leading to dry eyes and mouth. It can be primary (often associated with HLA.DR3) or secondary such in association with SLE. Due to the dry eyes this can lead to recurrent conjunctivitis and the dry mouth difficulty swallowing.

questions.question: A 28 year old female presents with joint pain in her wrists and hands. These are worst in the morning with significant morning stiffness. On examination there is evidence of active synovitis. What blood test should be performed?
questions.explanation: This patient most likely has RA. RF should be measured and is specific if the history is indicative although it can be positive in other autoimmune diseases. A positive RF is associated with a worse prognosis.

questions.question: A 32 year old female presents with muscle weakness. She is finding it difficulty to climb stairs and brush her hair. Over her knuckles there is erythematous scaly papules. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The history is in keeping with a myositis and the rash is Gottrons sign which is pathognomonic for dermatomyositis.

questions.question: A 32 year old female presents with muscle weakness. She is finding it difficulty to climb stairs and brush her hair. Over her knuckles there is erythematous scaly papuleg and a purplish rash around her eyes. What associated disease should be suspected?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is dermatomyositis. This can often be associated with a malignancy such as lung, oesophageal, breast, colon and ovarian tumors. Therefore patient should be monitored for this.

questions.question: A 39 year old male presents with proximal muscle weakness. He has been feeling generally unwell for several months. He has noticed a malar rash with a purplish rash around his eyes. There is erythematous scaly lesions on his arms. His CK is elevated. How do you make the definitive diagnosis?
options: A- CT Chest abdomen and Pelvis
questions.explanation: The history is suggestive of dermatomyositis. A definitive diagnosis is made by a muscle biopsy. If there is evidence of Gottrons papules and proximal muscle weakness this may avoid the need for a biopsy as these are pathognomonic. A CT CAP would only be indicated if you suspect an underlying malignancy. ANA and RF are not specific for the diagnosis.

questions.question: A 52 year old woman with previous history of IBS presents with general aches and pains all over with stiffness in her hands and wrist, not worse at any time of the day. She has been unable to sleep because of the pain and is very fatigued. She is also suffering from band like headaches. On examination there are multiple tender spots over her hips and back. Blood results including auto antibodies are normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Fibromyalgia is the most likely diagnosis. It leads to generalized musculoskeletal pain, stiffness, tenderness, sleep disturbance and easy fatigability. It usually affects woman from 30 to 60 years of age. Diagnostic criteria are set out but the ACR and include; widespread pain for 3 months; pain on palpation of certain trigger point e.g. greater trochanter, second rib, occiput; There is nil of note on examination and all blood investigations are normal.

questions.question: A 52 year old male presents with malaise, fever, headache and arthralgia. He complains of myalgia on exertion. He describes loss of sensation in his feet and notices his hands turn white and are painful in the cold. He is found to be hypertensive and a raised ESR. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is PAN. PAN is a vasculitis which affects medium sized vessels. It can affect multiple organ systems. It often presents with non specific features such as malaise etc, and then features of the systems affected such as peripheral neuropathy, mononeuritis multiplex, hypertension etc. There is a diagnostic criteria set out by the ACR. The features described are e not typical of RA> PMR is not associated with the neurological features.. SLE does not normally present in this way.

questions.question: What should patients be warned about whilst on Raloxifene?
options: A- Must be taken in the morning, an hour before food
C- Higher risk of breast cancer
questions.explanation: Raloxifene is a selective oestrogen receptor modulator and thus can increase the risk of developing a thromboembolic event. It can also lead to hot flushes, irregular vaginal bleeding, breast tendemess and leg cramps. Raloxifene increases bone density and reduces fracture risk at the spine.

questions.question: A 28 year old gentleman presents with severe low back pain. It has been present for several months and he s very stiff in the morning. He has been woken several times during the night with it. The pain is relieved by exercise. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The history and age of the patient suggests ankylosing spondylitis. The waking from night, morning stiffness and relief with exercise suggests this is an inflammatory pain rather than mechanical pain. The history is not indicative of a disc prolapse. He is unlikely to have an osteoporotic crush fracture given his age. Similarly he is unlikely to have metastatic disease. Spinal stenosis leads to similar symptoms to intermittent claudication and the pain is relieved by bending and is less severe ongoing uphill.

questions.question: What feature is indicative of gonococcal arthritis?
questions.explanation: Tenosynovitis is highly suggestive of Gonococcal arthritis. The other options are nonSpecific. It leads to a culture negative effusion. It usually begins as a polyarthritis then develops into a monoarthritis.

questions.question: How does psoriatic arthritis normally present?
options: A- Mono arthritis of the knee
E- Arthritis affecting the MCPs and PIPs
questions.explanation: The most common presentation is peripheral asymmetric oligoarthropathy. DIP disease is classical but accounts for a small minority of patients and arthritis mutilans even less.

questions.question: Which if these features is more indicative of a secondary Raynauds compared to a primary?
questions.explanation: In secondary Raynauds the formation of ulcers and gangrene are more common than in primary as is age greater than 50, being male, positive autoantibodies and asymmetric attacks.

questions.question: A 22 year old male is referred with a purpuric rash over his buttocks and lower legs. He has also notices some pain and swelling in his ankle, knees and wrists. He is also complaining of crampy abdominal pain. A dipstick of his urine reveals microscopie haematuria. He suffered a cold recently. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The features described are characteristic of Henoch Schönlein purpura. There is criteria for its diagnosis however it often leads to high levels of IgA and the most common presenting features are characteristic purpuric rash, abdominal pain, joint pain and microscopic haematuria and proteinuria. It is a vasculitis and is normally a disease of childhood. It can affect adults but has a poorer prognosis and leads to more severe renal involvement. It often follows a URTI. HUS leads to anaemia, thrombocytopenia and acute renal failure and often follows bloody diarrhoea such as E. Coli. You would expect in both Goodpastures and Wegeners to produce both pulmonary and renal symptoms and purpura is not a feature.

questions.question: A 70 year old female presents with shoulder and pelvic girdle pain. She is stiff for approximately 2 hours in the morning. She is feeling generally unwell. She has painful active movements of the shoulders and hips. Her ESR is markedly elevated whilst her CRP is normal. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is polymyalgia rheumatica. The history is indicative of PMR as is the raised ESR with normal CRP. It is classically the pelvic and shoulder girdles affected as the proximal muscles are affected. Polymyositis affects the proximal muscles but leads to weakness and pain is not really a feature. CK is elevated in polymyositis. Osteomalacia and osteoarthritis do not present in this way. These joints are not typically the ones affected by rheumatoid arthritis.

questions.question: A 42 year old Asian female presents with proximal muscle weakness and bony pain. She is found to have a low calcium and phosphate and a high ALP. An Xray of her femur shows loosers zones. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Osteomalacia is due to lack of vitamin D and is seen in Asian immigrants in this country.It leads to defective bone mineralization and thus symptoms of bone pain, muscle weakness and pathological fractures. Loosers zones and the blood findings are pathognomonic. Hypoparathyroidism leads to low calcium, normal phosphate and ALP levels and do not produce Loosers zones.

questions.question: A 28 year old known to have Raynauds phenomenon presents with painful, tight and swollen tips of fingers and a tight mouth. Anti-centromere antibodies are positive. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis which leads to the development of Raynauds followed by numerous years then development of skin changes, dysphagia and other features. Anticentromere antibodies are present. In diffuse there is more widespread systemic disease.

questions.question: A 30 year old with Rheumatoid arthritis presents with dry mouth and gritty eyes, What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Sjögrens syndrome leads to lymphocytic infiltration of the salivary and lacrimal glands leading to gritty eyes and dry mouth. It can be primary or secondary when it is associated with another autoimmune disease such as RA or SLE.

questions.question: A 60 year old gentleman presents with proximal muscle weakness and has noticed a rash on his knuckles and a purplish rash around his eyes. His CK is elevated. He also pdmits to having significant weight loss and a cough and haemoptysis. Which antibody would you expect to find?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is dermatomyositis. It is often associated with an underlying malignancy e.g. in this case likely an underlying lung cancer. It leads to proximal muscle weakness and heliotropic purplish rash and Gottrons papules (papules on knuckles) are characteristic. Anti Jo I are positive. Anticentromere is associated with scleroderma and anti CCP and RF with rheumatoid arthritis. Anti dsDNA is associated with SLE.

questions.question: A 23 year old presents with asthma and recurrent rhinitis develops purpura, right foot and wrist drop and bloods reveal acute renal failure, elevated eosinophils and pANCA positive. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Churg. Strauss syndrome is the most likely diagnosis and is a variant of polyarteritis nodosa. Classically it leads to rhinitis and asthma, eosinophilia and systemic vasculitis. le is a small vessel necrotising granulomatous disease which affects the lungs, peripheral nerves and skin. PANCA is associated. In PAN there is usually no rhinitis or asthma.known to occur and PANCA is negative. Wegeners leads to rhinitis and respirator features but not he skin and neurological changes observed here. Henoch Schönlein does not lead to the neurological or respiratory features but does lead to purpura.

questions.question: A 35 year old male with Crohns disease, who is currently having a flare, presents with a swollen painful right knee and raised bruise like lesions on his legs. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The most likely diagnosis is enteropathic arthritis. It is an acute asymmetrical inflammatory oligoarthritis which can occur in inflammatory bowel disease and normally afiects the lower limbs. Reiters syndrome is the triad of arthritis, conjunctivis and urethritis and can be associated with STI. Erythema nodosum is also described and is is associated with IBD.

questions.question: A 37 year old who has a long standing history of back pain and kyphosis is complaining of shortness of breath on exertion. There is crepitations at the apices of the lungs and X-ray of the spine shows ossification of the anterior longitudinal ligament and blurring of the sacroiliac joints. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: The diagnosis is Ankylosing spondylitis given the clinical feature sand X-ray findings. It can lead to apical fibrosis rarely and can also lead to dyspnoea secondary to kyphosis.

questions.question: A patient presents with recurrent dislocation of his shoulder. On examination he is hypermobile, has loose skin and you notice lots of bruising. What is the most likely diagnoses?
